75	  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
76	  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
77	  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
78	  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
79	  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
80	  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
81	  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
82	  (Bingcheng).
83	- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
84	  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
85	  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
86	  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
87	- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
88	  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
89	  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
90	  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
91	  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
92	- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
93	  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
94	  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
95	  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
96	  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
97	  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
98	  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
99	  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
100	- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
101	  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
102	  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.
103	
104	
105	## Silent preconditions
106	
107	Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
108	bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
109	each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
110	the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)
111	
112	| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
113	|---|---|---|---|
114	| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
115	| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
116	| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
117	| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |
118	
119	## Sweep stack & data layout
120	
121	The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
122	station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
123	`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
124	specifics:
125	
126	- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
127	  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
128	- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
129	  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
130	  any visual read.
131	- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
132	  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
133	  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.
134	
135	## Timing rules of thumb
136	
137	Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
138	current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
139	calibrating run.
140	
141	- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
142	  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
143	  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
144	  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
145	  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
146	  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
147	- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
148	  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
149	  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
150	  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
151	  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
152	- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
153	  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
154	- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
155	  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
156	  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
157	  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
158	- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
159	  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
160	  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
161	  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
162	- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
163	  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
164	  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
165	  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
166	  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
167	  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.
168	
169	## Standard equipment
170	
171	Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
172	hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.
173	
174	- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
175	  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
176	  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
177	  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
178	  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
179	  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
180	  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
181	  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
182	  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
183	- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
184	  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
185	  `measurement_config`.
186	- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
187	  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
188	  deterministic dV/dt); the
189	  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
190	  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
191	  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
192	  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
193	- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
194	  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
195	  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
196	  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
197	  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
198	  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
199	  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
200	  (read `mux.settle_s`).
201	  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
202	  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
203	  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
204	- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
205	  influx-logger kernel.
206	- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
207	  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
208	- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
209	  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.
210	
211	## Known quirks
212	
213	- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
214	  to address unicode issues.
215	
216	## What this card does not carry
217	
218	- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
219	  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
220	- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
221	- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
222	  device card + SAFETIES cell.
223	- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
224	  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
225	  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.


## Silent preconditions

Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)

| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |

## Sweep stack & data layout

The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
specifics:

- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
  any visual read.
- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

## Standard equipment

Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.

- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
  deterministic dV/dt); the
  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (read `mux.settle_s`).
  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
  influx-logger kernel.
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

## Known quirks

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

# === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12 cm^-2, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm; (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}); '
              f'B 0 -> 10 T uniform-B (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.sweep(magnet.field, B_vec, delay=0)
# gates stay at the spot; field stays at 10 T (the hole-side spot check rides it down) — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f})")

--- sdh_onset (R: 'np.ndarray', B: 'np.ndarray', *, b_hi: 'float | None' = None, b_lo: 'float' = 0.3, r_full_scale: 'float | None' = None, headroom: 'float' = 0.95, bg_degree: 'int' = 5, f_min: 'float' = 3.0, snr_threshold: 'float' = 5.0, n_periods: 'float' = 3.0, min_periods: 'float' = 2.0, step_frac: 'float' = 0.25, gap_widths: 'float' = 0.5, min_pts: 'int' = 8, max_tones: 'int' = 8, tone_floor_mult: 'float' = 4.0, marginal_mult: 'float' = 2.0) -> 'SdhOnset'
Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single Rxx trace.

    `R` is one longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`, `B` the matching field
    `(n_B,)` (arbitrary spacing). Removes a degree-`bg_degree` B-space
    polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT
    scans (`_tone_id`), then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter from
    high B down to where it sinks into the record's white-noise floor
    (`_track_tone` — a 5σ-style statistical onset, which legitimately sits
    below a by-eye read).

    Returns an `SdhOnset`; `onset_b` is the minimum onset over non-marginal
    tones — the `B_lo` a `landau-fan` design should use, correct even when a
    light tone outlives the dominant tone (per-dominant-tone semantics
    silently mis-served light-tone hunts). A tone still above threshold in
    its lowest window is *censored*: its onset is the recor
--- sdh_fft (R_grid: 'np.ndarray', B: 'np.ndarray', *, b_range: 'tuple[float, float] | None' = None, nfft: 'int' = 512, bg_degree: 'int | None' = 5, window: 'str | None' = 'hann', log: 'bool' = True, floor: 'float' = 1.0, uniform_rtol: 'float' = 0.1) -> 'tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]'
Per-column Shubnikov–de Haas FFT in 1/B.

    `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)` (rows = field, the `FanGrids` row axis); `B`
    is the per-row field `(n_B,)` — arbitrarily spaced. For each column:
    select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, remove a degree-
    `bg_degree` polynomial background in **B-space** (`None` skips), then take
    the FFT in 1/B. The background subtraction happens on the raw B axis
    *before* the 1/B step because the MR background is smooth in B, not 1/B.

    The 1/B resample is **conditional**. The field may be swept uniformly in
    1/B (then the samples are already evenly spaced in 1/B and are FFT'd
    directly, zero-padded to `nfft`) or uniformly in B (then the 1/B samples
    are resampled onto a regular `nfft`-point grid by interpolation against
    **sorted** 1/B). Which path is taken is decided from the actual 1/B
    spacing distribution (`un
--- luttinger_frequency (n: 'Any') -> 'np.ndarray'
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla.

    A single Fermi surface carrying the full density `n` gives this SdH
    frequency; the 4 is the spin×valley (4-fold) Landau degeneracy. `n` is in
    m^-2 (SI — feed `GateCalibration.density` output directly). Returns `|n|`
    form: the SdH frequency is positive for either carrier sign.
--- field_invB (B_start: 'float', B_end: 'float', N: 'int') -> 'np.ndarray'
Field axis of `N` points from `B_start` to `B_end`, uniform in 1/B.

    SdH oscillations are periodic in 1/B, so an FFT-bound field sweep samples
    evenly in 1/B (not in B). This is the measurement-side companion to
    `sdh_fft`'s uniform-1/B path: sweeping `field_invB` hands `sdh_fft` an
    already-even 1/B record (no resample). Argument order sets the sweep
    direction — high `B_start` descends, low `B_start` ascends.

    Both endpoints must be > 0 (1/B is taken). Returns `(N,)` Tesla.
--- open_run (path: 'str | Path') -> 'Run'
Open a sweep run directory — completed or in flight.

    `path` is the run dir (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Must contain
    `metadata.json` and either `data.tsv.gz` or `data.tsv`. Column names
    come from metadata — TSVs are headerless, and sweep writes `columns`
    to `metadata.json` at sweep start, so names resolve mid-run too. An
    in-flight run's TSV may end mid-row; only newline-terminated rows are
    trusted (sweep writes row-at-a-time, so interior lines are whole).

# Tetralayer FS-count forward model — ABAB vs ABCA (vs ABCB)

Backs the `recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

## Parameters and validity

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute
frequencies.** The discriminating outputs are the FS count, the ABAB partition
and its φ²-split masses, and the model-independent Luttinger sum
Σ±f = (h/4e)|n|. Absolute frequencies inherit the hopping-parameter error bars.

- **ABAB**: Koshino–McCann graphite SWMcC set {γ₀ = 3.0, γ₁ = 0.4, γ₂ = −0.02,

"""Runs 6 & 7 — sdh-spot-check reads (electron n=+3.2e12, hole n=-1.2e12, D=0).

Raw R(B), sdh_onset per trace, FFT vs F_L and the model F(n) table.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs

from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError

RUNS = {
    6: dict(n=+3.2e12 * 1e4, label="electron  n = +3.2e12", sens=50e-6),
    7: dict(n=-1.2e12 * 1e4, label="hole      n = -1.2e12", sens=50e-6),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8))
for row, (rid, spec) in enumerate(RUNS.items()):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    mc = r.meta["measurement_config"]
    ibias = None
    # I_bias from measurement_config (drive amplitude / bias R)
    for k, v in mc.items():
        print(rid, repr(k), repr(v)) if "bias" in str(k).lower() or "amp" in str(k).lower() or "gain" in str(k).lower() else None
    sr1_gain = mc.get("sr1_gain", 1)
    # drive: sr1 oscillator amplitude / 100 MOhm
    amp = None
    for k in mc:
        if "amplitude" in str(k).lower() or "excitation" in str(k).lower():
            amp = mc[k]
            print(rid, "amp key", k, amp)
    X = r.col("sr1_X")
    # R = (X / gain) / I_bias
    print(rid, "mc keys:", list(mc.keys()))
    # find I_bias
    ib_keys = [k for k in mc if "I" in str(k) or "bias" in str(k).lower()]
    print(rid, "ib candidates:", {k: mc[k] for k in ib_keys})

plt.close(fig)

--- resolve_channels (meta: 'dict[str, Any]', include: 'list[str] | None' = None) -> 'list[Channel]'
Resolve the lock-in `_X` columns of a run into `Channel`s.

    Gains and role labels come from `meta['measurement_config']`. `include`,
    if given, restricts to those channel ids (e.g. ['sr1','sr2']) or column
    names. Handles both rig namings (`sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain`, `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`).

--- resistance_grids (fan: 'FanGrids', channels: 'list[str] | None' = None) -> 'ResistanceGrids'
Per-channel resistance grids `R = (V/gain_V) / I` from a `FanGrids`.

    The denominator is the *measured* drain current `I = X_cur / gain_cur`
    (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a nominal bias
    current. Gains come from `measurement_config` (shared `resolve_channels`);
    nothing is hardcoded. Returned R is **signed** (X/I) — take `np.abs` for
    Rxx magnitude, keep the sign for Rxy/Hall. `channels` restricts the
    voltage channels returned (the current channel is always resolved).

--- current_channel (channels: 'list[Channel]') -> 'Channel | None'
The single transimpedance current channel, or None if not exactly one.

    The measured drain current (gain-divided) is the denominator of the
    four-probe resistance R = V / I — see `resistance_grids`.

"""Runs 6 & 7 — sdh-spot-check reads (electron n=+3.2e12, hole n=-1.2e12, D=0).

Raw R(B) first, then sdh_onset per trace, FFT vs F_L and the model F(n) table.
R = (sr1_X/gain) / (sr0_X/gain)  — measured drain current denominator.
"""
import sys

import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_onset, sdh_fft,
    luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError,
)

RUNS = {
    6: dict(n_cm2=+3.2e12, label="run 6 — electron, n = +3.2e12, B 0→10 T"),
    7: dict(n_cm2=-1.2e12, label="run 7 — hole, n = −1.2e12, B 10→0.3 T"),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 9))
results = {}
for row, (rid, spec) in enumerate(RUNS.items()):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    chans = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    cur = current_channel(chans)
    vch = [c for c in chans if c is not cur and c.column == "sr1_X"][0]
    I = r.col(cur.column) / cur.gain
    R = (r.col(vch.column) / vch.gain) / I
    order = np.argsort(B)
    B, R, I = B[order], R[order], I[order]

    n_SI = spec["n_cm2"] * 1e4
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(n_SI))

    # model tones at this density (F, kF) / (F_total,...)
    _, abab = fs.abab_fs(spec["n_cm2"] / 1e12)
    _, _, _, _, F_abca = fs.abca_fs(spec["n_cm2"] / 1e12)
    abab_F = [f for f, _ in abab]

    # onset
    try:
        onset = sdh_onset(R, B)
        onset_b = onset.onset_b
        tones = [(t.frequency, t.onset_b, getattr(t, "censored", None)) for t in onset.tones]
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        onset, onset_b, tones = None, None, str(e)

    # FFT above onset (fall back to 1.5 T)
    b_lo = onset_b if onset_b else 1.5
    f_ax, P = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(b_lo, B.max()), nfft=4096, log=False)
    P = P[:, 0]

    results[rid] = dict(F_L=F_L, abab=abab_F, abca=F_abca, onset=onset_b,
                        tones=tones, R0=R[np.argmin(np.abs(B - B.min()))],
                        Rmax=np.nanmax(np.abs(R)))
    print(f"=== {spec['label']} ===")
    print(f"  F_L = {F_L:.1f} T | model ABAB tones {['%.1f' % f for f in abab_F]} | ABCA {F_abca:.1f} T")
    print(f"  R({B.min():.2f} T) = {R[0]:.1f} Ω, |R|max = {np.nanmax(np.abs(R)):.1f} Ω, I_bias med = {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.2f} nA")
    print(f"  onset_b = {onset_b}")
    if onset is not None:
        for t in onset.tones:
            print(f"    tone: {t}")

    ax = axes[row, 0]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ω)"); ax.set_title(spec["label"] + " — raw")

    ax = axes[row, 1]
    m = B >= max(b_lo * 0.8, 0.5)
    bg = np.polyval(np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5), B[m])
    ax.plot(1.0 / B[m], R[m] - bg, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("ΔRxx (Ω)")
    ax.set_title(f"detrended, B ≥ {max(b_lo*0.8,0.5):.2f} T")

    ax = axes[row, 2]
    ax.plot(f_ax, P, lw=0.8, label=f"FFT B∈[{b_lo:.2f},{B.max():.1f}] T")
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="k", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L = {F_L:.1f} T")
    for f in abab_F:
        ax.axvline(f, color="tab:red", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.axvline(F_abca, color="tab:green", ls="-.", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(F_L * 1.6, 50)); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT|")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
    ax.set_title("red: ABAB model, green: ABCA model")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png")

"""Runs 6 & 7 — sdh-spot-check reads (electron n=+3.2e12, hole n=-1.2e12, D=0).

Raw R(B) first, then sdh_onset per trace, FFT vs F_L and the model F(n) table.
R = (sr1_X/gain) / (sr0_X/gain)  — measured drain current denominator.
"""
import sys

import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_onset, sdh_fft,
    luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError,
)

RUNS = {
    6: dict(n_cm2=+3.2e12, label="run 6 — electron, n = +3.2e12, B 0→10 T"),
    7: dict(n_cm2=-1.2e12, label="run 7 — hole, n = −1.2e12, B 10→0.3 T"),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 9))
results = {}
for row, (rid, spec) in enumerate(RUNS.items()):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    chans = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    cur = current_channel(chans)
    vch = [c for c in chans if c is not cur and c.col == "sr1_X"][0]
    I = r.col(cur.col) / cur.gain
    R = (r.col(vch.col) / vch.gain) / I
    order = np.argsort(B)
    B, R, I = B[order], R[order], I[order]

    n_SI = spec["n_cm2"] * 1e4
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(n_SI))

    # model tones at this density (F, kF) / (F_total,...)
    _, abab = fs.abab_fs(spec["n_cm2"] / 1e12)
    _, _, _, _, F_abca = fs.abca_fs(spec["n_cm2"] / 1e12)
    abab_F = [f for f, _ in abab]

    # onset
    try:
        onset = sdh_onset(R, B)
        onset_b = onset.onset_b
        tones = [(t.freq, t.onset_b, t.censored) for t in onset.tones]
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        onset, onset_b, tones = None, None, str(e)

    # FFT above onset (fall back to 1.5 T)
    b_lo = onset_b if onset_b else 1.5
    f_ax, P = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(b_lo, B.max()), nfft=4096, log=False)
    P = P[:, 0]

    results[rid] = dict(F_L=F_L, abab=abab_F, abca=F_abca, onset=onset_b,
                        tones=tones, R0=R[np.argmin(np.abs(B - B.min()))],
                        Rmax=np.nanmax(np.abs(R)))
    print(f"=== {spec['label']} ===")
    print(f"  F_L = {F_L:.1f} T | model ABAB tones {['%.1f' % f for f in abab_F]} | ABCA {F_abca:.1f} T")
    print(f"  R({B.min():.2f} T) = {R[0]:.1f} Ω, |R|max = {np.nanmax(np.abs(R)):.1f} Ω, I_bias med = {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.2f} nA")
    print(f"  onset_b = {onset_b}")
    if onset is not None:
        for t in onset.tones:
            print(f"    tone: {t}")

    ax = axes[row, 0]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ω)"); ax.set_title(spec["label"] + " — raw")

    ax = axes[row, 1]
    m = B >= max(b_lo * 0.8, 0.5)
    bg = np.polyval(np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5), B[m])
    ax.plot(1.0 / B[m], R[m] - bg, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("ΔRxx (Ω)")
    ax.set_title(f"detrended, B ≥ {max(b_lo*0.8,0.5):.2f} T")

    ax = axes[row, 2]
    ax.plot(f_ax, P, lw=0.8, label=f"FFT B∈[{b_lo:.2f},{B.max():.1f}] T")
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="k", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L = {F_L:.1f} T")
    for f in abab_F:
        ax.axvline(f, color="tab:red", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.axvline(F_abca, color="tab:green", ls="-.", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(F_L * 1.6, 50)); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT|")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
    ax.set_title("red: ABAB model, green: ABCA model")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png")

"""Runs 6 & 7 — sdh-spot-check reads (electron n=+3.2e12, hole n=-1.2e12, D=0).

Raw R(B) first, then sdh_onset per trace, FFT vs F_L and the model F(n) table.
R = (sr1_X/gain) / (sr0_X/gain)  — measured drain current denominator.
"""
import sys

import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_onset, sdh_fft,
    luttinger_frequency, SdhOnsetError,
)

RUNS = {
    6: dict(n_cm2=+3.2e12, label="run 6 — electron, n = +3.2e12, B 0→10 T"),
    7: dict(n_cm2=-1.2e12, label="run 7 — hole, n = −1.2e12, B 10→0.3 T"),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 9))
results = {}
for row, (rid, spec) in enumerate(RUNS.items()):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    chans = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    cur = current_channel(chans)
    vch = [c for c in chans if c is not cur and c.col == "sr1_X"][0]
    I = r.col(cur.col) / cur.gain
    R = (r.col(vch.col) / vch.gain) / I
    order = np.argsort(B)
    B, R, I = B[order], R[order], I[order]

    n_SI = spec["n_cm2"] * 1e4
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(n_SI))

    # model tones at this density (F, kF) / (F_total,...)
    _, abab = fs.abab_fs(n_SI)
    _, _, _, _, F_abca = fs.abca_fs(n_SI)
    abab_F = [f for f, _ in abab]

    # onset
    try:
        onset = sdh_onset(R, B)
        onset_b = onset.onset_b
        tones = [(t.freq, t.onset_b, t.censored) for t in onset.tones]
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        onset, onset_b, tones = None, None, str(e)

    # FFT above onset (fall back to 1.5 T)
    b_lo = onset_b if onset_b else 1.5
    f_ax, P = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(b_lo, B.max()), nfft=4096, log=False)
    P = np.asarray(P).reshape(-1, len(f_ax))[0]

    results[rid] = dict(F_L=F_L, abab=abab_F, abca=F_abca, onset=onset_b,
                        tones=tones, R0=R[np.argmin(np.abs(B - B.min()))],
                        Rmax=np.nanmax(np.abs(R)))
    print(f"=== {spec['label']} ===")
    print(f"  F_L = {F_L:.1f} T | model ABAB tones {['%.1f' % f for f in abab_F]} | ABCA {F_abca:.1f} T")
    print(f"  R({B.min():.2f} T) = {R[0]:.1f} Ω, |R|max = {np.nanmax(np.abs(R)):.1f} Ω, I_bias med = {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.2f} nA")
    print(f"  onset_b = {onset_b}")
    if onset is not None:
        for t in onset.tones:
            print(f"    tone F={t.freq:6.2f} T  contrast={t.contrast:7.1f}  onset={t.onset_b:.2f} T"
                  f"  censored={t.censored}  marginal={t.marginal}  near_res={t.near_residual}"
                  f"  harmonic_of={t.harmonic_of}")

    ax = axes[row, 0]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ω)"); ax.set_title(spec["label"] + " — raw")

    ax = axes[row, 1]
    m = B >= max(b_lo * 0.8, 0.5)
    bg = np.polyval(np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5), B[m])
    ax.plot(1.0 / B[m], R[m] - bg, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("ΔRxx (Ω)")
    ax.set_title(f"detrended, B ≥ {max(b_lo*0.8,0.5):.2f} T")

    ax = axes[row, 2]
    ax.plot(f_ax, P, lw=0.8, label=f"FFT B∈[{b_lo:.2f},{B.max():.1f}] T")
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="k", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L = {F_L:.1f} T")
    for f in abab_F:
        ax.axvline(f, color="tab:red", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.axvline(F_abca, color="tab:green", ls="-.", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(F_L * 1.6, 50)); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT|")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
    ax.set_title("red: ABAB model, green: ABCA model")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/spots_runs67.png")

"""Landau-fan design numbers (investigation step 2/4 + landau-fan step 1).

2. Model F(n) table over the electron-side fan window (light-tone resolvability).
3. Grid: Delta(1/B) Nyquist at n_max, n-axis ray Nyquist at B_lo, deltaF, cost.
"""
import sys
import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs
from hera.analysis import luttinger_frequency, field_invB

# --- measured fundamentals (sdh_onset, runs 6/7; harmonics screened Luttinger-aware) ---
meas = {
    +3.2e16: (7.11, 22.08),   # electron spot: light, heavy (22.08 un-flagged: dropping it breaks the sum)
    -1.2e16: (4.72, 6.59),    # hole spot: close balanced pair
}

# 1. single global density rescale s: model pair at s*n vs measured pair
def model_pair(n_SI):
    _, orbs = fs.abab_fs(n_SI)
    Fs = sorted(f for f, _ in orbs)
    return Fs

def cost(s):
    c = 0.0
    for n, (fl, fh) in meas.items():
        Fs = model_pair(s * n)
        if len(Fs) < 2:
            return np.inf
        c += ((Fs[0] - fl) / fl) ** 2 + ((Fs[-1] - fh) / fh) ** 2
    return c

# 2. model F(n) over candidate electron window (as-calibrated densities)
print("\nmodel ABAB F(n) [electron side, at calibrated n, and at s*n]:")
print(" n(cal,e12)   F_light  F_heavy   F_light@s  F_heavy@s   F_L")
for n12 in (1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.2):
    n = n12 * 1e16
    Fs = model_pair(n)
    Fss = model_pair(s_best * n)
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(n))
    a = f"{Fs[0]:7.2f} {Fs[-1]:8.2f}" if len(Fs) >= 2 else f"  {Fs}   "
    b = f"{Fss[0]:8.2f} {Fss[-1]:9.2f}" if len(Fss) >= 2 else f"  {Fss}    "
    print(f"  {n12:5.1f}     {a} {b} {F_L:8.1f}")

# masses for the LK step later
for n12 in (2.0, 3.2):
    print(f"m*(n={n12}e12):", [(round(f, 1), round(m, 3)) for f, m in fs.abab_mstar(n12 * 1e16)])

# 3. grid design
B_max = 10.0
F_fast = float(luttinger_frequency(3.2e16))          # fastest expected tone: F_L at n_max (scale-1, conservative)
for B_lo in (0.5, 0.7, 1.0):
    d_invB = 1.0 / (3.0 * F_fast)                    # 3 samples/period (prefer-1/3 Nyquist)
    span = 1.0 / B_lo - 1.0 / B_max
    N_B = int(np.ceil(span / d_invB)) + 1
    dF = 1.0 / span
    dn_ray = 4 * 1.602e-19 / 6.626e-34 * B_lo / 1e16  # ray spacing in 1e12 cm^-2 at B_lo
    print(f"\nB_lo={B_lo}: Delta(1/B)={d_invB:.5f} -> N_B={N_B}, deltaF={dF:.2f} T, "
          f"ray Dn@B_lo={dn_ray:.3f}e12 -> n-step <= {dn_ray/2:.3f}e12")

# candidate: n 1.2 -> 3.2, N_n from ray floor at chosen B_lo
for (B_lo, N_B) in ((0.7, None),):
    pass

"""Runs 6 & 7 — sdh-spot-check (electron n=+3.2e12, hole n=-1.2e12, D=0): raw, onset, FFT vs model."""
import sys
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/hera/measurement_env/hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count")
import fs_count_b0 as fs
from hera.analysis import (open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel,
                           sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency)

RUNS = {6: +3.2e16, 7: -1.2e16}   # n (SI, m^-2) at D = 0, run-5 calibration


def rxx(rid):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    ch = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    cur = current_channel(ch)
    v = [c for c in ch if not c.is_current][0]
    R = (r.col(v.col) / v.gain) / (r.col(cur.col) / cur.gain)
    o = np.argsort(B)
    return B[o], R[o]


fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8.5))
onsets = {}
for row, (rid, n_SI) in enumerate(RUNS.items()):
    B, R = rxx(rid)
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(n_SI))
    _, orbs = fs.abab_fs(n_SI)
    _, _, _, _, F_abca = fs.abca_fs(n_SI)

    # onset on the clean 10 mT record (>= 1 T) for run 6; full record for run 7 (20 mT throughout)
    b_lo_rec = 1.0 if rid == 6 else 0.3
    onset = sdh_onset(R[B >= b_lo_rec - 1e-9], B[B >= b_lo_rec - 1e-9], b_lo=b_lo_rec)
    onsets[rid] = onset
    print(f"run {rid}: n = {n_SI/1e16:+.1f}e12, F_L = {F_L:.1f} T | ABAB model "
          f"{[f'{f:.1f}' for f, _ in orbs]} T, ABCA {F_abca:.1f} T | onset_b = {onset.onset_b:.2f} T")
    for t in onset.tones:
        if t.contrast > 50:
            print(f"  F = {t.freq:5.2f} T  contrast {t.contrast:6.1f}  onset {t.onset_b:.2f} T"
                  f"  censored={t.censored}  harmonic_flag={t.harmonic_of}")

    ax = axes[row, 0]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    ax.set_title(f"run {rid} raw — n = {n_SI/1e16:+.1f}e12, D = 0")

    ax = axes[row, 1]
    m = B >= 0.55
    bg = np.polyval(np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5), B[m])
    ax.plot(1 / B[m], R[m] - bg, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)"); ax.set_title("detrended (deg-5 in B)")

    ax = axes[row, 2]
    b_fft = max(onset.onset_b, 0.7)
    f_ax, P = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(b_fft, B.max()), nfft=4096)
    P = np.asarray(P).reshape(-1, len(f_ax))[0]
    ax.plot(f_ax, P, lw=0.8)
    ax.axvline(F_L, color="k", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L = {F_L:.1f} T (g=4)")
    for f, _ in orbs:
        ax.axvline(f, color="tab:red", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.axvline(F_abca, color="tab:green", ls="-.", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(1.6 * F_L, 50)); ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("|FFT| (log-R detrend)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.set_title(f"FFT B in [{b_fft:.2f}, 10] T — red ABAB / green ABCA model")

fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# --- global density-rescale pin (Verify: single scale fit to the WHOLE tone set) ---
meas = {+3.2e16: (7.11, 22.08),   # heavy tone un-flagged: dropping it as a 3.1x harmonic breaks the Luttinger sum
        -1.2e16: (4.72, 6.59)}

def cost(s):
    c = 0.0
    for n, (fl, fh) in meas.items():
        Fs = sorted(f for f, _ in fs.abab_fs(s * n)[1])
        if len(Fs) < 2:
            return np.inf
        c += ((Fs[0] - fl) / fl) ** 2 + ((Fs[-1] - fh) / fh) ** 2
    return c

ss = np.arange(0.80, 1.01, 0.01)
s_best = ss[int(np.argmin([cost(s) for s in ss]))]
print(f"\nglobal density rescale s = {s_best:.2f} (lever-arm prior band 0.8-1.2)")
for n, (fl, fh) in meas.items():
    F_L = float(luttinger_frequency(abs(n)))
    Fs = sorted(f for f, _ in fs.abab_fs(s_best * n)[1])
    print(f"  n = {n/1e16:+.1f}e12: measured ({fl:.2f}, {fh:.2f}) sum {fl+fh:.1f} = {(fl+fh)/F_L:.2f} F_L,"
          f" partition {fl/(fl+fh):.2f}/{fh/(fl+fh):.2f} | ABAB model at s*n: ({Fs[0]:.1f}, {Fs[-1]:.1f})")

from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD
from hera.analysis import field_invB

# --- session calibration (run 5, cnp-and-dline-calibration) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)

# --- fast axis: paired n-line at D = 0, ray-Nyquist floor at B_lo = 0.7 T (n-step 0.033e12 <= 0.034e12) ---
N_N = 61
ns = np.linspace(1.2, 3.2, N_N)                  # 1e12 cm^-2
Ds = np.zeros(N_N)
Vtgs, Vbgs = calc_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtgs.min() and Vtgs.max() <= TG_MAX, (Vtgs.min(), Vtgs.max())
assert BG_MIN <= Vbgs.min() and Vbgs.max() <= BG_MAX, (Vbgs.min(), Vbgs.max())
print(f"n-line: {N_N} pts, n = {ns[0]:+.2f} -> {ns[-1]:+.2f}e12 at D = 0; "
      f"Vtg {Vtgs.min():+.4f}..{Vtgs.max():+.4f} V, Vbg {Vbgs.min():+.4f}..{Vbgs.max():+.4f} V")

# --- slow axis: uniform 1/B, Delta(1/B) = 0.0101 = 1/(3*F_L(n_max)) (3 samples/period at F = 33.1 T) ---
N_B = 133
B_vec = field_invB(0.7, 10.0, N_B)               # ascending: starts near the magnet (0 T), ends at 10 T
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: fan ascends from 0.7), "
      f"V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# Fixed sensitivity 100 uV = 10 kOhm FS at 10 nA: worst corner is low-n x 10 T (run 7 anchor 587 Ohm at
# |n|=1.2e12, 10 T -> ~6% FS; headroom over QH spikes beats resolution — clipping corrupts a whole column FFT).
sr1.sensitivity(100e-6)
I_TRIP = 1e-9
print(f"B rows: {N_B}, {B_vec[0]:.2f} -> {B_vec[-1]:.1f} T (dB 5 mT -> 0.9 T); sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, "
      f"tau {sr1.time_constant()} s; fast_delay 1.8 s = 6 tau")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan electron side: n = +1.20 to +3.20e12 ({N_N} pts), D = 0 (run-5 cal), "
                  f"B 0.7 -> 10 T uniform-1/B ({N_B} rows), sr1 100 uV")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = +1.20 to +3.20e12 cm^-2 ({N_N} pts, D = 0), B = 0.70 -> 10.00 T uniform-1/B '
              f'({N_B} rows, d(1/B) = 0.0101); Vtg {Vtgs.min():+.4f}..{Vtgs.max():+.4f}, Vbg {Vbgs.min():+.4f}..{Vbgs.max():+.4f}; '
              f'cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}; '
              f'design from runs 6/7: scale 0.90, tones 7.1/22.1 (e) 4.7/6.6 (h)')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbgs[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtgs[0])
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, Vtg, Vbg, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")

The fan's per-column FFT turns that one-density read into the F(n) trajectory: partition robustness f₁+f₂ = 0.9·F_L(n) across density, branch labeling on the model curves (dual overlay vs trilayer), and the n-dependence screen that decides whether 22.1 T is the ABAB heavy tone or a 3× harmonic — the fork the whole call hangs on.
